To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the concept class of halfspaces can be learned privately over the real line; (b) the class of decision trees can be learned privately on the Boolean hypercube; and (c) the class of linear separators can be learned privately in the presence of noise over the real line.

(1) private learning is possible for a broad class of concept classes, including all PAC-learnable concept classes and many more; (2) private learning is as hard as PAC learning for the class of halfspaces in R^d, and (3) private learning is impossible for the class of monotone halfspaces in R^n, and the class of linear threshold functions in R^n.
